sense: something by which one finds the way

terms.gloss: a mark; with locī or locōrum, a landmark
terms.grammar: usually plural, with the genitive locī or locōrum
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.174: sī signa et notās ostenderem locōrum
terms.comment: Cicero’s signa et notae locōrum are the marks by which a place is found again, the landmarks one points out to someone who must find the spot alone. The o is short: nota “a mark”, not nōta “known”. In giving directions Latin seldom needs the word: it names the thing and asks whether the hearer knows it (Nōstīn' porticum apud macellum hāc deorsum?, Ter. Ad. 573), and goes on with ubi eō vēneris and ubi … praeterieris.

terms.gloss: a sign, a mark to know a place by
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.174: signa et notās … locōrum
terms.comment: Joined with nota in Cicero’s phrase; on its own signum is as often a statue or a signal, so nota is the clearer word.

phrases.latin: satis esse dēbēret, sī signa et notās ostenderem locōrum, quibus cognitīs ipse sibi foderet
phrases.english: it ought to be enough if I showed him the signs and landmarks of the places; once he knew them, he could dig for himself

phrases.latin: est urbe ēgressīs tumulus templumque vetustum dēsertae Cereris, jūxtāque antīqua cupressus religiōne patrum multōs servāta per annōs; hanc ex dīversō sēdem veniēmus in ūnam
phrases.english: as you leave the city there is a mound and an old temple of Ceres, now deserted, and beside it an ancient cypress kept for many years by our fathers’ reverence; to this one spot we shall all come by different ways

phrases.latin: scīn' Cratīnī hujus dītis aedēs? — Sciō. — Ubi eās praeterieris, ad sinistram hāc rēctā platēā; ubi ad Diānae vēneris, ītō ad dextram
phrases.english: Do you know the house of rich Cratinus here? — I do. — When you’ve passed it, go left, straight along this street; when you get to Diana’s temple, turn right

phrases.latin: Haec turris nōbīs prō notā erit; ubi eam cōnspexerimus, nōn longē ā domō aberimus.
phrases.english: This tower will be our landmark; once we catch sight of it, we won’t be far from home.

sources: Lewis & Short: nota · Lewis & Short: signum
